reason: Both conversations correctly steered the homeowner to inspect the coupler and asked for the model number, but Conversation 1 clearly named the cracked, rounded piece as the turntable coupler, explained why it causes the fault, and gave a correct cheap clip-on replacement route (manufacturer spares / authorised centre with the model number) plus unplugged fitting instructions. Conversation 2 ended with a muddled, hedging summary ('turning alongside a broken coupler or roller ring', 'would need testing'), never confirmed the coupler as the fix despite the customer having described it, and escalated to an engineer for a trivial user-replaceable part, which is unnecessary and costly. Conversation 2 did lead with a slightly stronger unplug-first safety line, but Conversation 1 maintained adequate casing-removal warnings throughout.
